newsitem.title: USA: N.J. officials rally for $1.1 bln rail -- paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. officials rally for $1.1 bln rail -- paper.

text.p: Supporters of a proposed $1.1 billion light-rail system for southern New Jersey staged a rally to counter growing opposition to the idea, the Philadelphia Inquirer reported Tuesday.
City officials from eight Burlington County towns discounted recent setbacks for the plan, including votes in Palmyra and Riverton Borough withdrawing support.
Opponents have expressed concerns about safety along the tracks, and the rail line's effect on traffic and crime, the newspaper said.

NJ Transit voted last year to proceed with preliminary work on the line, and has spent nearly $40 million on initial contracts. The agency's board has scheduled a January vote on awarding contracts for construction and operation.
